key_insight: BrickWright argues that AI agents can create physically valid LEGO builds that match user prompts when equipped with assembly tools and physical-feasibility checks.
problem_solved: AI-generated 3D designs can look plausible while containing floating, overlapping, or disconnected pieces, making them unsuitable for real-world assembly.
method: Focus on LEGO brick builds as a concrete testbed for physically constrained 3D creation.
Provide agents with tools for assembling brick-based designs.
Verify physical feasibility to help agents avoid invalid arrangements while preserving the requested design.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a route from visually convincing generation to physically buildable outputs: pair capable agents with domain-specific construction and verification tools. The supplied abstract is incomplete and does not report quantitative results.
visual_elements: Side-by-side brick builds: floating or overlapping pieces versus a connected, feasible assembly.
Workflow diagram: user prompt → AI agent → assembly tools → feasibility checks.
Three constraint icons highlighting floating, colliding, and disconnected bricks.

paper_title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
paper_authors: Ava Pun, Kevin Dai, Sally Chen, Maxwell Jones, Ruixuan Liu
